name: SnappyData
tagline: In-memory HTAP database fused into Apache Spark executors; acquired by TIBCO and now unmaintained.
description: SnappyData embedded a transactional in-memory row and column store, derived from GemFire/Apache Geode, inside Apache Spark executors, so one cluster could ingest streams, apply point updates and serve SQL analytics without copying data between Spark and a separate database. It added approximate query processing on sampled synopses and exposed JDBC, ODBC, REST and the Spark APIs. TIBCO acquired the company in 2019 and sold it as TIBCO ComputeDB; the last release, 1.3.1 in June 2022, still targets Spark 2.1.1. The repository is now marked as legacy with no updates, security fixes included, so it is only relevant for existing installations.
statusNote: TIBCO (owner since 2019) stopped updates after 1.3.1 (June 2022); the repo is legacy-only with no security fixes. Consider Spark SQL with a lakehouse, Apache Ignite or ClickHouse.

pricing.notes: Community Edition was Apache 2.0; TIBCO sold the commercial edition as TIBCO ComputeDB.

scale.notes: Data is partitioned across Spark executors and held mostly in memory, so cluster RAM bounds hot data.

strengths: Database and Spark share one cluster and memory, avoiding data movement between them
Mutable row and column tables with point updates, which plain Spark lacks
Approximate query processing for fast answers over very large tables
Streaming ingest and SQL analytics in the same engine
weaknesses: Discontinued: no updates or security patches after 2022
Pinned to Spark 2.1.1, years behind current Spark
Memory-heavy clusters are expensive to run
Complex to operate compared with today's lakehouse stacks
useCases: Maintaining existing SnappyData or ComputeDB clusters
notIdealFor: Workloads that need current Spark versions
